pairs.subject: drag-drop
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/spatial-stash/SpatialStashGrid.tsx:88 The drop handler takes identity from ambient drag state instead of the received payload, allowing stale intent to authorize an unrelated drop.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/spatial-stash/SpatialStashPalette.tsx:92 The palette publishes an untyped text ID; the receiving grid accepts from ambient intent without inspecting a declared transferable kind.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/spatial-stash/SpatialStashGrid.tsx:211 Source dragend clears intent while drop separately clears target hover; no common reaper handles both resources or clears module-level intent on unmount.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/spatial-stash/SpatialStashGrid.tsx:148 The grid provides a red/green footprint preview only after dragover sets hover; valid destinations do not announce themselves at drag start.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/spatial-stash/SpatialStashGrid.tsx:111 The only stash-grid key operation rotates existing intent; no keyboard or click alternative creates or repositions a placement, and drag transitions lack live announcements.

src/stores/spatialInventoryStore.ts:125 Explicit drop coordinates bypass placement validation in the owning store, and placePlacement unconditionally appends; collision and bounds checks remain in the gesture handler against its tab snapshot.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/spatial-stash/SpatialStashGrid.tsx:88 Stable IDs exist, but onDrop never reads dataTransfer.getData and instead authorizes placement using the singleton's identity.
